name: Boltwood’s radioactive geological age estimates
description: Boltwood published geological age estimates using radioactive change, an early quantitative approach to deep time.

impact.note: First ages of rocks from radioactive decay; geologists gained a quantitative deep time, and radiometric geochronology grew from it.

date.basis: Year of the cited publication or dated report; not necessarily the date work began.

events.statement: Boltwood published a list of geological ages based on radioactivity in 1907.

evidence.supports: Dates Boltwood’s list of radioactive geological ages to 1907.
Describes the limits of his chemical uranium–lead dates.

contributions.resource: Contributed to the documented Boltwood’s radioactive geological age estimates work.

evidence.supports: Dates Boltwood’s list of radioactive geological ages to 1907.

earliest_record.rationale: A dated witness within the evidence collected here; not a claim of global priority or earliest observation.

caveats: These early chemical ages were revised; they preceded accurate decay constants and modern isotope-resolved methods. Rutherford and other researchers contributed earlier ideas.

research.note: Independent source reading checked the dated events and associated claims. Grain and other facets remain provisional.
